name: FORTIS INC.

ads_ratio.source: Fortis Inc. Form 40-F / FY2025 annual report: the Corporation's common shares are listed directly on the TSX and NYSE under the symbol FTS (release header: TSX/NYSE: FTS); there is no depositary or ADS program — the NYSE line is the same common shares.
ads_ratio.reason: Direct-listed ordinary (common) shares on both exchanges, so per-share figures from the filings and the NYSE price are on the same share basis: ratio 1.0.

fx_conversion.source: frankfurter.app — ECB reference rates (closest business day to each period end)

overrides_applied.source: Fortis Inc. FY2025 consolidated financial statements (filed with the Form 40-F for the year ended Dec 31, 2025), Note 20 Stock-Based Compensation Plans: PSU compensation expense recognized C$109M (2025) and RSU compensation expense recognized C$41M (2025); DSU expense stated not material; stock options fully vested at Dec 31, 2025 with no expense figure disclosed. Total disclosed stock-based compensation expense FY2025 = C$150M (CAD, as filed; the engine FX-converts at period-end rates).
overrides_applied.reason: EDGAR companyfacts carries no SBC figure for Fortis under any candidate tag (ShareBasedCompensation, AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, ifrs AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments) for any filed year — sbc_tag is blank for 2016-2025 — so the v5 data gate gaps SBC for FY2023-2025. Fortis discloses the expense only in Note 20 of its financial statements. A single override value fills every untagged year, so the latest filed year (FY2025, C$150M) is used for all years: it overstates FY2024 (disclosed total C$82M = PSU C$53M + RSU C$29M), i.e. it errs in the conservative direction (more SBC = lower owner's earnings), and the amount is immaterial against the deeply negative OE base either way.

fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CAD converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Fortis Inc. Form 40-F / FY2025 annual report: the Corporation's common shares are listed directly on the TSX and NYSE under the symbol FTS (release header: TSX/NYSE: FTS); there is no depositary or ADS program — the NYSE line is the same common shares.) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Fortis Inc. FY2025 consolidated financial statements (filed with the Form 40-F for the year ended Dec 31, 2025), Note 20 Stock-Based Compensation Plans: PSU compensation expense recognized C$109M (2025) and RSU compensation expense recognized C$41M (2025); DSU expense stated not material; stock options fully vested at Dec 31, 2025 with no expense figure disclosed. Total disclosed stock-based compensation expense FY2025 = C$150M (CAD, as filed; the engine FX-converts at period-end rates).); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
note: No positive NORMALIZED (3-yr median) conservative owner's earnings — OE DCF not supportable on numbers alone. If the latest year alone is positive, that is a flag to investigate, not a pass.

override_impact.basis: engine-native normalized base (median of last 3 FY) and weighted IRR, DCF run both ways (zero-fill baseline vs with-override); a --base-oe-ps TTM base is excluded from both sides — its override effect shows in ttm.py output
